_comment: One line covering a whole vendored package - the thing a developer shipping dozens of files from one release actually wants, and the thing our own vendor-ambiguous-source response tells them to write. Before this, a directory source could only be a github /tree/ URL: pointed at a CDN the fetch SUCCEEDED (those URLs answer 200 with an HTML listing page), the unzip failed, and every file under lib/ was recorded unfetchable - reviewed as the developer's own code, and REJECTED where minified. Now the pkg@version is taken off the URL and the package's own registry tarball answers for the directory. The network map serves only that tarball, so nothing here could pass by accident: no file URL is listed. LICENSE.txt is the point of the directory form - it is covered without being named, which a file declaration cannot do. Its bytes are published in the package, so it verifies with the rest; membership, not path, is what a directory declaration can ask, since it names one source for many files.
